findings.text: Meta followed a three-pronged trust and safety strategy: enable safe developer use, protect against adversarial users, and provide community protections against misuse.

source.quote: we followed a three-pronged strategy to managing trust & safety risks:

findings.text: Safety fine-tuning used the same mitigations as Llama 3 and stressed refusals to benign prompts and refusal tone, including borderline and adversarial prompts.

source.quote: We implemented the same set of safety mitigations as in Llama 3

findings.text: Meta says Llama 3.2 should not be deployed alone and should use system safeguards such as Llama Guard, Prompt Guard, and Code Shield.

source.quote: Large language models, including Llama 3.2, **are not designed to be deployed in isolation**

findings.text: For chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear, and explosive weapons (CBRNE), Meta points to Llama 3.1 70B/405B uplift testing and says that testing also applies to the smaller 1B and 3B models.

source.quote: have determined that such testing also applies to the smaller 1B and 3B models.

findings.text: Child Safety work used expert assessments and red teaming across attack vectors and languages during Llama 3 development, then applied to this release.

source.quote: We leveraged those expert red teaming sessions to expand the coverage of our evaluation benchmarks through Llama 3 model development.

findings.text: Cyber work cited for this card is uplift and ransomware-style attack-automation testing on Llama 3.1 405B, which Meta broadly treats as applying to Llama 3.2 1B/3B.

source.quote: For Llama 3.1 405B, our cyber attack uplift study investigated whether LLMs can enhance human capabilities in hacking tasks

findings.text: Pretraining used knowledge distillation: logits from Llama 3.1 8B and 70B were token-level targets after pruning.

findings.text: The card states testing to date has not covered all scenarios and outputs can be inaccurate, biased, or objectionable.

source.quote: Testing conducted to date has not covered, nor could it cover, all scenarios.
